messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info

message.content: We don’t have a definitive “largest planet” in the entire universe—our knowledge is limited to what we can observe from Earth and our solar system. Within our own Solar System, Jupiter is the biggest planet, with a diameter of about 142,000 km. Among the thousands of exoplanets discovered so far, the largest confirmed ones are gas giants that are several times larger than Jupiter, such as HD 100546 b (about 7–10 Jupiter radii) and WASP‑17b (roughly 1.8 Jupiter radii but extremely low density). However, many of the very large candidates are still under study, and it’s possible that even bigger planets exist beyond our current detection limits.
